question: A sum of money becomes seven times in 16 years at simple interest per annum. Find the per annum rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate (R) = [(n − 1) × 100] ÷ Time

Here, n = 7 (times) and Time = 16 years.

R = [(7 − 1) × 100] ÷ 16

R = (6 × 100) ÷ 16 = 600 ÷ 16 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 7 × Principal (P)

Time (T) = 16 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 
• 
 
 
 
 Principal (P)
 Year 0
 
 Amount (7P)
 Year 16
 

 SI = 6P

⇒ Let the Principal (P) be ₹100.

⇒ Amount (A) = 7 × 100 = ₹700.

⇒ Simple Interest (SI) = A − P = 700 − 100 = ₹600.

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 600 = (100 × R × 16) ÷ 100

⇒ 600 = 16 × R

⇒ R = 600 ÷ 16

⇒ R = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

General Formula for n-times growth

If a sum becomes n times in T years, the rate is R = (n − 1) × 100 ÷ T. Conversely, the time required is T = (n − 1) × 100 ÷ R.

Simple Interest vs Amount

Simple Interest remains constant every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal. Amount = Principal × [1 + (R × T ÷ 100)].

Compound Interest comparison

In Compound Interest, a sum becomes n times in T years, then it will become n² times in 2T years and n³ times in 3T years.
